fix_commit_message:
Add NULL check in ossl_quic_get_peer_token

If a peer address hasn't been set on a quic channel yet, we will not
yield a token from our hashtable of available tokens.  Fail the
get_peer_token lookup in that event

Fixes #27608

Reviewed-by: Saša Nedvědický <sashan@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/27610)
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 99ea6b38430d on top of intro 9a055c89170b via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The function ossl_quic_get_peer_token calls ossl_quic_build_new_token(peer, NULL, 0) to create a lookup key, but does not check if the returned key is NULL before using it in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve(). When the peer address hasn't been set on a QUIC channel yet (as happens early in connection establishment in the http3 demo), ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL because BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on the uninitialized peer. The NULL key is then passed to lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve which dereferences it, causing a segmentation fault. Root cause: The ossl_quic_get_peer_token function was introduced without proper error handling for the case where ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL. The ossl_quic_build_new_token function returns NULL when BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on the peer parameter, which occurs when the peer address hasn't been set on the QUIC channel yet. The code proceeds to use this NULL key in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve without checking.
